description: Composite surface-topography figure of SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel, made of ten images grouped as five sample conditions (a)–(e) = P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130 and P-150, each condition pairing a colour-coded 2D height map with a 3D rendered surface (nearest taxonomy type: AFM-like 3D topography/roughness; the large 0–600 µm field suggests a profilometer rather than true AFM). The 2D maps have x and y axes in µm spanning about 0–600 µm plus a vertical height colour bar in µm; the 3D panels add a z height scale and a max-height label. Legible 3D height labels are 144.6 µm (first panel), 86.3 µm, 49.51 µm and 36.05 µm (fourth panel); the fifth 3D label is unreadable. The colour scale runs dark blue (low) → green → yellow → orange → red/white (high). The first panel shows large coalesced orange/red–white plateaus, whereas the later panels become predominantly blue with isolated red spikes, so relief visibly decreases panel by panel. The figure demonstrates that raising laser power from 70 W to 150 W progressively smooths the SLM surface, with Sa falling from 20.71 µm (P-70) to 4.19 µm (P-150) per the citing text. The caption lists Sa values in a scrambled order relative to the panel letters.

subfigures.description: Colour-coded 2D height map of P-70, x/y axes about 0–600 µm, dominated by large orange, red and white/pink plateaus in the lower half over a green/yellow background, indicating the roughest surface in the group. No colour bar visible (cropped).

3D rendered surface of the same sample with a µm colour bar (0, 50, 100, …) and a z/maximum-height label of 144.6 µm; shows a tall red mesa and a large pink/white hill, the highest relief of the five 3D panels.
2D height map of P-90 with axes about 0–600 µm; yellow-green field with a deep blue elongated depression centre-left and small red spots near the bottom edge. Colour bar not visible in the crop.
3D surface rendering with a µm colour bar (0–80) and z/maximum-height label 86.3 µm; intermediate relief with several reddish peaks on a green-blue base.
2D height map of P-110 with axes about 0–600 µm and a colour bar scaled to about 0–40 µm; mostly cyan-green with a diffuse orange patch left-of-centre and small red/yellow highs.
3D surface rendering with a µm colour bar (0–40) and z/maximum-height label 49.51 µm; smoother, rippled surface with green-yellow crests and blue troughs.
2D height map of P-130 with axes about 0–600 µm; predominantly blue-cyan with dark blue vertical bands and a red/white spot near the top edge. Colour bar not visible.
3D surface rendering with a µm colour bar (0–35) and z/maximum-height label 36.05 µm; low-relief undulating surface with fine ripples and mostly blue-green colouring.
2D height map of P-150 with axes about 0–600 µm and a colour bar reaching about 50 µm; largely deep blue/cyan with orange-red patches on the right side and a printed ‘Sa’ label above the frame.
3D surface rendering of the final condition, mostly dark blue (low relief) with a single red peak at the upper-right corner; z height label not legible at the supplied resolution.

observations.observation: The figure contains ten sub-images: five colour-coded 2D height maps alternating with five 3D rendered surface topographies, forming five sample conditions.
The 2D maps are plotted with x and y axes in µm spanning approximately 0–600 µm on both axes.

The 3D panels carry a z height scale with printed maximum-height labels: first panel 144.6 µm, third 86.3 µm, fifth 49.51 µm and seventh 36.05 µm in reading order; the label of the last 3D panel is unreadable.
The height colour scale runs from dark blue (low) through green, yellow and orange to red/white (high), with units of µm.
Surface relief visibly decreases from the first panel, which shows large coalesced orange/red–white plateaus, to the last panels, which are predominantly deep blue with only isolated red spikes.
The figure shows 2D and 3D topographies and surface roughnesses of the SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloys for (a) P-70, (b) P-90, (c) P-110, (d) P-130 and (e) P-150.
The surface of the SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy became smoother with increasing laser power.
P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130 and P-150 exhibited surface roughness values of 20.71, 9.19, 5.29, 4.65 and 4.19 µm, respectively.
A low surface roughness is beneficial for printing high-precision components, whereas excessive surface roughness affects the dimensional accuracy of a printed sample.

The caption text that lists Sa values is scrambled relative to the panel letters (it prints ‘Sa=4.65 μm (a) Sa=20.71 µm (b) Sa=9.19 μm (c) Sa=5.29 μm (d) (e) Sa=4.19 μm’), so the Sa-to-panel mapping is not reliable from the caption alone.
A printed ‘Sa’ value label appears above the 2D map of the final condition, but the associated panel letter is not legible.
